name: Groombridge 1618
description: A nearby orange dwarf, 64% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured by interferometry.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 380: radius in solar radii, 0.6398 +/- 0.0046, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 380: mass 0.66 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 380: effective temperature in K, 4085 +/- 14, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists

text.card: A nearby orange dwarf whose disc was measured by interferometry: 64% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Interferometry gives it 0.6398 solar radii; with its total light, that makes its surface 4,085 K.
